text.p: - Russia's former security chief, Alexander Lebed, on a private visit in France cancelled his appointment to see Napoleon's tomb but put some time to climb the Eiffel Tower.
- Izvestia lists allegations of wrongdoing by Sergei Mavrodi, founder of the collapsed MMM financial pyramid scheme, during the life of his money-making enterprise. Mavrodi has denied any wrongdoing.
- Several hundred tonnes of oil have poured out onto the ground and into a nearby river from a ruptured pipeline near Saratov in the south of Russia.
- Irish beef exporters assure Russian buyers that no "mad cow" meat will find its way onto the Russian market.
- President Boris Yeltsin's meetings with Defence Minister Igor Rodionov and border guards commander Andrei Nikolayev did not produce any surprising news.
- Tajik field commander Bakhrom Sadirov frees unharmed all the international hostages he was holding.
- A blazing fire in the centre of Moscow was put out just in time to save a huge nearby cigarette factory from annihilation.
- Important changes at the top of the defence ministry and the general staff could come as early as March.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin should be more resolute in his refusal to meet the opposition's calls for him to step into the president's shoes at the first possible opportunity.
- Russia is about to make another attempt to go ahead with its long-overdue military reform.
